findings.claim: The S3/lemmaR_tight framing is oversold: the separation theorem operates at fixed defect depth delta with bandwidth L >= C·delta^{-1}(log log t + log(1/delta)), while lemmaR_tight's indistinguishability — and every ceiling-relevant adversary — lives in the depth -> 0 regime, where the first-order system is equally blind at any finite bandwidth.
findings.argument: The tight-pair corollary separates an on-line double at t from an off-line pair at (t, delta) with margin ~ delta^2 e^{delta L}, requiring L >= C·delta^{-1}(log log t + log(1/delta)). As delta -> 0 at any fixed L, the discriminating quantity 2ghat(t) - 2Re ghat(t - i·delta) = -delta^2 · d^2/dy^2 Re ghat(t-iy)|_{y=0} + O(delta^4) is O(delta^2 L^2 · sup|ghat|) -> 0, so pairs at depth delta << 1/L are invisible to ALL bandwidth-L first-order data. But lemmaR_tight (TightMult.lean) states precisely that the double and the pair AT DEPTH -> 0 are indistinguishable (both charge 4), and the 256-periodic ceiling law uses marks in {1,2} (on-line doubles) or depth-epsilon pairs. Therefore the corollary does not 'do exactly what lemmaR_tight proves impossible' in the regime where the tightness theorem and the ceiling bind; it extends the data class to be depth-sensitive at FIXED depth — a genuine but strictly weaker capability. The honest statement: bandwidth-one two-moment data is depth-blind at every depth ('an off-line pair enters ONLY through the signature of its hyperbolic block, regardless of |beta-1/2|', per the map), whereas first-order bandwidth-L data resolves depth down to ~ (log log t)/L. The proposal's phrasing 'does exactly what lemmaR_tight proves impossible' should be replaced by this calibrated claim; as written a referee of the eventual paper would flag it as a scope error.

findings.claim: Milestone M5 (coupling moves the 0.6818 ceiling's scope) is predictably vacuous, not open: an adversarial law matching bandwidth-one pair data AND bandwidth-L first-order data with 1/3 non-simple zeros exists by sub-resolution perturbation, because linear statistics are multiplicity-blind below scale 1/L.
findings.argument: First-order sum-rule data at bandwidth L, Sum_Z ghat(gamma) for supp g in [-L,L], determines the configuration measure only after smoothing at scale 1/L, and is LINEAR in the measure. Two consequences: (a) a double at t is exactly indistinguishable from two simples at t ± eps for eps << 1/L (difference ~ eps^2 sup|ghat''| ~ eps^2 L^2 sup|ghat| -> 0), so first-order rules impose NO constraint on multiplicity structure; (b) perturbing the 256-periodic law's atom positions by o(1/L) reproduces any target smoothed density (e.g. zeta's actual explicit-formula data A(g) - Int g d(pi)) while changing the bandwidth-one form factor S(j) at frequencies <= 1 only by O(shift · frequency) = o(1), within the enclosure tolerance after re-solving the LP. For the on-line-proportion side, the adversary replaces doubles by off-line pairs at depth delta = e^{-L}, whose first-order cost delta^2 e^{delta L} is astronomically below any threshold. Hence the joint system (first-order bandwidth-L + second-order bandwidth-one Gram) admits essentially the same extremal laws as the Gram system alone, and 'any strict exclusion moves the 0.6818 ceiling's scope' will not occur. The proposal half-admits this as failure mode 6 but prices M5 as a genuine open question consuming months 10-20; the argument above closes it in the negative before the work starts. REPAIR: restate M5 as proving this coupling no-go formally — a publishable ceiling theorem for the enriched data class, buildable with the existing Stability.lean/LawN256 LP template (the map explicitly says ceiling_stability re-runs against ANY candidate law), and honest evidence that the field's value is confined to the fixed-depth/single-defect regime.

findings.claim: Field-coherence gap: the flagship first theorem consumes neither axiom P (Lambda >= 0) nor the conservation system — it is a pure statement about two abstract configuration classes and one bandlimited test function — while the sector that does consume the celebrated positive-prime-measure input (Sector I) is expected, by the proposal's own calibration, to saturate at the classical zero-free region.
findings.argument: Inspect the first theorem's statement: hypotheses are (i) reflection/conjugation symmetry, (ii) RvM local density, (iii) window membership (Z' real in window, Z = defect orbit + real). The conclusion bounds |Sum_Z ghat - Sum_{Z'} ghat| from below by an explicit test construction. No prime measure, no archimedean functional, no explicit formula appears: this is bandlimited interpolation theory (Phragmen-Lindelof growth e^{yL}, Gevrey decay, derivative-bump construction). The 'conservation-law field' dressing enters only when one wants to CONCLUDE something about zeta — which requires knowing which class zeta's data falls in, i.e., the M6 detector, gated by pointwise short-Euler-product control that the proposal itself concedes may be provably out of reach (almost-periodicity lower bounds). Meanwhile the Lambda >= 0 thesis — 'the input the entire L2/Weil-positivity industry provably never uses' — is load-bearing only in Sector I's budget partition, and failure mode 2 plus the DMV-Beurling calibration honestly predict Sector I's ceiling is (near-)exactly the classical dlVP region, i.e., no progress into the strip interior. So the novelty rhetoric and the provable deliverable live in different sectors: the provable sector doesn't use the new input; the sector using the new input is expected not to beat 1899-1958 technology except in constants. This does not refute the proposal but substantially lowers its payoff-per-theorem; the foundations paper (M1) should state this division of labor explicitly rather than letting the thesis paragraph imply the first theorem exploits positivity.

findings.claim: Sector I's novelty is narrower than claimed: the mu_y kernel is a classical table transform, and the positivity-LP-over-nonnegative-trig-polynomials approach to zero-free regions is established literature (Mossinghoff-Trudgian 2015, Mossinghoff-Trudgian-Yang, Kadiri); the genuinely new part is the compact-support/bandwidth grading, strip-depth kernels, and abstract-datum calibration — a new combination, not a new object.
findings.argument: The closed form F[cosh(yu)/cosh(u/2)](xi) = c·cos(pi y)cosh(pi xi)/(cosh(2pi xi)+cos(2pi y)) follows by scaling from the standard pair F[cosh(bv)/cosh(v)] = pi·cos(pi b/2)cosh(pi xi/2)/(cosh(pi xi)+cos(pi b)) (Gradshteyn-Ryzhik 3.981-family); positivity for |b|<1 is immediate. Presenting this as a discovery ('verified numerically to machine precision') rather than a citation weakens the paper. The LP over the cone {w >= 0, what >= 0} generalizing 3-4-1 is the direct explicit-formula analogue of the finite-dimensional optimization over nonnegative trigonometric polynomials that Mossinghoff-Trudgian ran for ZFR constants in 2015 and that the explicit-ZFR community (Kadiri, MTY) has iterated since; the proposal correctly flags this as its highest prior-art risk but schedules the search implicitly inside M1. The Boas-Kac/Cohn-Elkies cone structure is also exactly the object Carneiro-Milinovich-Ramos (arXiv:2310.01913, correctly cited, conditional use) deploy. Verdict on the novelty axis: Sector I = repackaging-plus-extension of known machinery (the extension being real: bandwidth grading, depth kernels mu_y, defect-cost LP V(t,y;L), Beurling-datum calibration); Sector II and the abstract separation theorem are new relative to PUBLISHED literature (their only antecedent is the campaign's own unpublished transcript Theorem 2, which the first theorem improves on two axes). REPAIR: do the prior-art search as milestone M0, before writing M1, and cite the transform.

findings.claim: Missing Siegel-zero calibration: within the axiom class (positive datum P + functional-equation-type archimedean term), the cone machinery has a PROVEN single-defect hole at the real axis — the Landau-Page exceptional zero — which should be built into M1/M3 as an internal no-go and which further supports the expectation that Sector I saturates at classical technology.
findings.argument: The datum pi_chi = sum Lambda(n)(1+chi(n)) n^{-1/2}(...) for a real primitive character chi is a POSITIVE measure with Chebyshev growth (coefficients Lambda(n)(1+chi(n)) >= 0), and zeta(s)L(s,chi) satisfies an exact degree-2 functional equation, so (pi_chi, A_chi) is an admissible datum in the proposal's abstract class (with its own archimedean functional). The classical Landau-Page analysis IS the cone argument applied to this datum, and it famously CANNOT exclude a single simple real zero near s=1: the positivity budget is exactly consumed, and only Siegel's ineffective argument (importing input beyond P+FE) improves it. Hence 'single-defect sensitivity' of the termwise-positive sector provably fails for at least one defect location within the axiom system — a sharper internal calibration than the DMV-Beurling one the proposal already includes (Beurling worlds test the value of FE; the Siegel datum tests the cone's limits WITH an exact FE present). Incorporating this costs nothing and pre-empts the most obvious expert objection ('we tried positivity-only single-defect exclusion in 1918-1935; its limit is the exceptional zero'). It also predicts the answer to M3's LP question near the real axis: the cone ceiling there is exactly the Landau-Page region, not better.

findings.claim: Corollary T2 (localization) is false as stated: certified positivity of u on the single segment {sigma = a, |t| <= T} does NOT imply quasi-RH(a) up to collars, because negativity plumes of moderately deep zeros never reach the line sigma = a.
findings.argument: Around an off-line zero rho0 = beta + i*gamma0 with beta > a, the negative term of the master identity at s = a + i*gamma0 is -(beta-a)/((beta-a)^2 + 0) = -1/(beta-a), while the ambient positive contribution of on-line zeros at that point is ~ pi * d(gamma0) = (1/2) log(gamma0/2pi) (Poisson-summing density d = log(gamma0/2pi)/2pi against the kernel (a-1/2)/((a-1/2)^2+y^2)). So u(a, gamma0) <= 0 requires 1/(beta-a) > (1/2) log(gamma0/2pi), i.e. beta - a < 2/log(gamma0/2pi). A zero at depth beta = a + 0.1 at height 10^100 (2/log ~ 0.009 << 0.1) leaves u(a, .) strictly positive on the whole line sigma = a: its plume lives at sigma near beta, not at sigma = a. This matches the proposal's own plume-width estimate in failure mode 3 (width ~ 1/((beta-a) log gamma)) — which contradicts T2 two pages earlier. Independent confirmation via the integral identity: integrating u(a,t) over t in (0,T) gives each zero ~ +pi if beta < a and ~ -pi if beta > a, so Int_0^T u(a,t) dt ~ pi [N(T) - 2 N_{>a}(T)] + O(edge); pointwise positivity on ONE segment therefore yields only the COUNTING bound N_{>a}(T) <= N(T)/2 + O(edge/2pi), never emptiness — an o(N)-type conclusion, ironically the blindness the proposal claims to escape. REPAIR: state T2 on 2D boxes {a <= sigma <= 1, |t| <= T} (there positivity IS equivalent to zero-freeness, since any interior zero forces u < 0 just to its left, inside the box), or on a sigma-grid of segments with spacing c/log T; and record the single-line integral identity separately as a legitimate counting/zero-density instrument (it is actually a nice unnoticed hook). M3's deliverable already says 'boxes', so the program survives; the first-theorem PACKAGE as written contains a false corollary a referee would bounce.

findings.claim: The novelty section misses its true nearest neighbors: the tilt family E_a(z) = xi(a - iz) with Hermite-Biehler/de Branges structure is substantively present in M. Suzuki's canonical-systems program and Lagarias 2006, and the u-positivity reformulation of RH exists in modulus form (Sondow-Dumitrescu 2010; Matiyasevich-Saidak-Zvengrowski). Mechanism is a new COMBINATION plus 2-3 new instruments, not a new object or new field.
findings.argument: (a) Since d/dsigma log|xi(sigma+it)| = Re xi'/xi(sigma+it) = u, Lagarias's positivity criterion is IDENTICAL to 'RH iff |xi| is increasing in sigma on every horizontal half-line sigma > 1/2' — which is Sondow-Dumitrescu (Period. Math. Hungar. 60, 2010), catalogued as a standard RH equivalent in Broughan's 'Equivalents of the Riemann Hypothesis' Vol. 2; Matiyasevich-Saidak-Zvengrowski proved adjacent unconditional horizontal-monotonicity results. The negativity body N is exactly the non-monotonicity set of these papers; 'no publication studies the geometry of {Re xi'/xi <= 0}' is at best half-true. (b) Masatoshi Suzuki has a decade-long program (e.g. 'A canonical system of differential equations arising from the Riemann zeta-function'; 'Hamiltonians arising from L-functions in the Selberg class', arXiv ~1606.05726 — flagged from memory, must be verified) that studies precisely shifted xi-functions xi(shift - iz) as de Branges structure functions, proves HB unconditionally for shift >= 1, characterizes RH as HB for all shifts > 1/2, and constructs the associated Hamiltonians — i.e. the 'tilt family' and its first rung already exist in print with a canonical-system theory built on top. The proposal cites only Suzuki arXiv:2301.00421 (a different, RH-conditional paper). (c) The Krein-Langer negative-squares count for Theta_a is folklore in the Kaltenbaeck-Woracek Pontryagin-de-Branges school. What genuinely appears unclaimed in the literature: the effective anchoring theorem, the height-resolved index-ladder bookkeeping, depth-direction complete monotonicity as a constraint class, and the OS_kappa axiomatization. REPAIR: rewrite the novelty section around these four differentiators and cite the neighbors; the differentiators plausibly survive, but a referee at a journal WILL know Suzuki's work and the current text would read as unaware of the closest prior art.

findings.claim: The Pontryagin (finite negative index) framing of the ladder is unconditionally vacuous on (1/2,1) and outright wrong for the validation models: kappa_a is not known to be finite for ANY a < 1, and for Davenport-Heilbronn/Epstein (h>1) kappa_a is INFINITE at rung one.
findings.argument: Krein-Langer/Pontryagin machinery (finite kappa negative squares, k-dimensional defect/ghost space in the M2 OS reconstruction, index monotonicity with jumps = multiplicities) presupposes kappa_a < infinity. Unconditionally, for every a in (1/2,1), the number of zeta zeros with beta > a is not known to be finite — zero-density gives only N_{>a}(T) = o(T), and infinitude is consistent with current knowledge; so the unconditional object is an extended-integer ladder on which 'jump formula' and 'defect space' have no content until truncated. Worse, the M2 milestone proposes to 'validate the axioms on Davenport-Heilbronn as an indefinite model with kappa > 0 at rung one' — but DH (and Epstein with h > 1) have INFINITELY many zeros in sigma > 1 (Davenport-Heilbronn 1936; Titchmarsh Ch. X), so their K_a lives in a genuinely infinite-negative-index Krein space where the entire Pontryagin toolbox (finite-defect OS reconstruction, Sylvester-inertia bookkeeping via RHLinalg on finite sections converging to kappa) does not apply as described. REPAIR: define the ladder height-truncated, kappa_a(T) := #{rho : beta > a, |gamma| <= T} (finite by RvM), state index monotonicity/jump formulas for truncations with T-uniform error control, and reposition DH as an infinite-index Krein model rather than a Pontryagin one. Fixable, but it restructures the M2 axiom system and removes some of the elegance the proposal sells (the clean 'kappa_a-dimensional ghost space').

findings.claim: The miracle (M4, margin propagation) is the classical zero-free-region wall renamed, and its falsifiable success criterion ('reprove a Vinogradov-Korobov-shaped region by pure TRP') is likely ill-posed: VK strength cannot come from the stated generators.
findings.argument: The proposal's generators are (G1) OS-Schwarz/reflection positivity for theta_a transported by the damping semigroup and (G2) depth-CM from Lambda >= 0 — i.e. inputs derivable from FE + Hadamard + Euler-product coefficient positivity. The rung-one engine is 3-4-1 trigonometric positivity, which is exactly the de la Vallee Poussin input, and dlVP-strength (c/log t) is the known ceiling of that input class; Vinogradov-Korobov regions require cancellation in Sigma n^{-it} (Vinogradov's mean-value / exponential-sum machinery), which is information about additive structure of log n that no amount of positivity/monotonicity in (Lambda >= 0, FE) supplies — a 'pure TRP' derivation of VK would have to smuggle Vinogradov in through the archimedean/prime-side estimates, at which point the reproof is a translation, not a new mechanism. The proposal's own failure mode 1 concedes the arithmetic of descent (~(1/2) log t archimedean drift per unit of a-descent, 'Lindelof-adjacent'), and its design confidence for M4 is 0.1/3y. As referee I price it lower: probability of BEATING any known ZFR by 3 years <= 0.05, and the honest M4 criterion should be split into (i) dlVP-shaped region by pure TRP (meaningful, plausible, a genuine proof-of-concept that the axioms carry analytic content) and (ii) VK-shaped with declared imports (specify exactly which exponential-sum input is admitted). Without this split, M4's kill criterion cannot actually be adjudicated. Note this is a pricing/honesty finding, not a refutation: unlike the canon's formalized ceilings, no obstruction THEOREM bars the route — history does the pricing, and the proposal is largely honest about it.

findings.claim: The depth-CM generator (G2) is overclaimed 'by construction': total monotonicity of the prime side in a requires the window's cosine transform to be nonnegative at the points log n, which fails for general windows w >= 0.
findings.argument: a |-> Sigma_{n<=X} Lambda(n) g-hat(log n) n^{-a} is a totally monotone (completely monotone) function of a iff all coefficients Lambda(n) g-hat(log n) >= 0. Lambda(n) >= 0 holds, but g-hat = cos-transform of w takes negative values for generic nonnegative w (w >= 0 does not imply w-hat >= 0). The CM/Hausdorff-Bernstein-Widder constraint class must be restricted to positive-definite windows (Bochner class: w = |v|^2-type autocorrelations, Fejer kernels etc.), which is still rich but strictly smaller than 'every fixed window', and the M3/numerics-(3) LP must be formulated inside that cone or it will impose false constraints. One-line repair, but it belongs in the immutable mechanism text and slightly shrinks the advertised transversality of the CM coordinate.

findings.claim: The first theorem is true and provable, but the sketched constants fail at all accessible heights: with current explicit S(t) bounds, a window of length H0 ~ 1.5 is NOT guaranteed to contain >= c0 log t0 zeros until astronomically large t0; and my tractability estimate is HIGHER than the designer's.
findings.argument: RvM gives count(t0-H0, t0+H0) = (H0/pi) log(t0/2pi) + O(1) - [S-fluctuation up to 2|S|]. With Trudgian-type |S(t)| <= 0.112 log t + 0.278 loglog t + 2.51 (or Hasanalizade-Shen-Wong 0.1038 log t + ...), the fluctuation term 2*0.112 log t0 + ~5 exceeds the H0 = 1.5 main term (1.5/pi) log(t0/2pi) ~ 0.477 log t0 - wait, at H0 = 1.5 interpreted as total window LENGTH 1.5 the main term is 0.239 log t0 < 0.224 log t0 + 5 for all t0 below ~e^300; even on the generous half-width reading the additive constant ~5-6.4 kills positivity for all t0 <= 10^3-10^5. The fix is trivial — take H0 ~ 10-15 (C1 scales linearly with H0) plus a verified-computation patch for 30 <= t0 <= 10^3 — and the proposal's failure mode 5 anticipates degradation, but the sketch's numbers as written do not close. Otherwise the proof architecture is sound: FE-pairing makes every pair whose deeper member has beta <= sigma0 contribute nonnegatively (checked: for beta >= 1/2, both (sigma0-beta) and (sigma0-1+beta) >= 0 when beta <= sigma0), window pairs each give >= (2 sigma0 - 1)/(H0^2 + 4) ~ c*delta, and the negative tail from zeros with beta > sigma0 at distance > R is <= C2 log t0 / R by the standard density Sigma_{|gamma - t0| > R} 1/|s0-rho|^2 << log t0/R. This is classical toolkit (Hadamard + effective RvM + Landau-type partial fractions, the same device used inside every ZFR proof); a strong group proves it in months, not 2 years. Designer's 0.55-within-months is roughly right; over a 2-year horizon I put it at 0.8-0.85 vs designer 0.6 — the direction UNDER-claims tractability here, unusual and to its credit, but the standalone weight of the theorem is correspondingly modest: a quantitative two-sided version of a folklore device, a solid lemma-paper, not a field-founding cornerstone.

findings.claim: The 'margin law m(a,60) ~ 0.046(a-1/2)' numerics are presented as evidence for the ladder but are mathematically trivial and, as a law, a small-T artifact.
findings.argument: In the RH-verified range every term of u(a,t) = Sigma m_rho (a-beta)/|s-rho|^2 is positive, so u(a,t) >= (a-1/2)/((a-1/2)^2 + dist(t, nearest gamma)^2); for t in (1,60) the largest nearest-zero distance is O(5-7) (the gap below gamma_1 = 14.13), giving min_t u ~ (a-1/2) * 0.04-0.05 exactly as observed. Linearity in (a-1/2) is forced termwise and tests nothing about propagation, CM, or RP. Moreover for FIXED a > 1/2 and T -> infinity, u(a,t) ~ pi * density = (1/2) log(t/2pi) at generic heights and the minimum over gaps GROWS like log T (nearest zero within pi/log t), so 'm(a,T) ~ 0.046(a-1/2)' is not a stable law. Similarly u(sigma, gamma_1) = 1/(sigma-1/2) is the bare nearest-term identity. findings.claim: The 'master formula' (tilted explicit formula), the field's declared identity backbone, is mathematically false exactly in the presence of what it is designed to detect: it omits residue terms from zeros above the level a.
findings.argument: The proposal states: for a > 1/2 and any window w with hat-w supported in [-log X, log X], Sigma_rho m_rho Int P_{a-beta}(t-gamma) w(t) dt = Arch_a(w) - Sigma_{n<=X} Lambda(n) n^{-a} (cos-transform w)(log n). Contour check: Int w(t) zeta'/zeta(a+it) dt is evaluated by shifting the line Re s = a to Re s = 2 (w entire by Paley-Wiener). Crossing poles of zeta'/zeta at zeros with beta > a contributes residues -2*pi*m_rho*w(gamma_rho - i(beta_rho - a)); the s=1 pole gives an explicit term. So the correct identity is: Poisson zero-sum = Arch_a(w) - Sigma_{n<=X} Lambda(n) n^{-a} w-hat_cos(log n) - 2*pi*Sigma_{beta>a} m_rho Re w(gamma_rho - i(beta_rho - a)). Consistency proof of the omission: the prime/archimedean side is real-analytic in a, but the Poisson term for a single zero, a |-> Int P_{a-beta}(t-gamma) w dt, has a genuine jump of 2*pi*m*w(gamma) at a = beta (limits +/- pi * Poisson-average of w; the odd function x/(x^2+y^2) has no analytic continuation through x=0). An analytic function cannot equal a jump-discontinuous one, so equality fails on (1/2, beta) for every zero with beta > a. I verified this numerically (Gaussian window, planted zero at 0.85 + 40i): Poisson branch jumps -3.1291 -> +3.1291 across a = 0.85 while adding the residue term 2*pi*Re w(gamma - i(beta-a)) restores the smooth continuation (3.1291 -> 3.4812 smoothly down to a = 0.6). Consequences: (1) the proposal's planned validation ('verify tilted EF against direct zero-side evaluation to 10+ digits') runs on true zeta in the verified range where all beta = 1/2 < a, i.e. precisely the case with no residues, so the error passes the planned test silently and propagates into the M3 LP, whose feasible set (configurations 'matching windowed tilted-EF data') is then wrong; any LP-certified 'zero-free box' from it is unsound. (2) The repair is known and standard, but it changes the field's story: with the residue restored, the tilted EF at level a with window w IS the ordinary Weil explicit formula with test g_a(u) = w-hat(u) e^{(1/2-a)u}, and off-line zeros enter with the classical X^{beta-a} amplification -- the 'Poisson pricing of every zero' narrative and the 'locality is cheap, X ~ e^{2pi}' claim both collapse into the classical explicit-formula game.

findings.claim: The core ceiling-evasion claim (S5) -- that the field reads 'a data coordinate (sigma-profiles) the bandwidth-one certificate model does not even parametrize' -- is false at the data level: the tilted-EF data at all levels a is exactly the ordinary band-limited Weil-EF prime data, reweighted.
findings.argument: The prime-side functional at level a with window w is Sigma_{n<=X} Lambda(n) n^{-a} w-hat(log n) = Sigma_n [Lambda(n)/sqrt(n)] * g_a(log n) with g_a(u) := w-hat(u) e^{(1/2-a)u}, supported in [-log X, log X]. The whole two-parameter family (a, w) therefore factors through the SAME finite data vector (Lambda(n))_{n<=X} paired against tests supported in [-log X, log X] -- precisely the band-limited test class of Weil positivity and the two-thirds certificate at bandwidth log X / log(T/2pi). The 'depth direction' is literally an exponential weight e^{(1/2-a)u} on the same test space; 'depth-direction complete monotonicity' of a |-> Sigma Lambda(n) g-hat(log n) n^{-a} is equivalent to Lambda(n) >= 0 and nothing more (a finite exponential sum with nonnegative coefficients is trivially totally monotone; conversely CM for all localized windows recovers Lambda >= 0 coefficientwise), so the Hausdorff-Bernstein-Widder constraints across the a-grid add zero information beyond the single constraint Lambda >= 0 already consumed at rung one. What actually differs from the capped certificate class is the FUNCTIONAL type (pointwise/linear positivity of u instead of quadratic form-factor pairings) -- so the formalized PairCeiling/lemmaR_tight theorems indeed do not formally apply, but for the wrong reason: the method escapes the post-Montgomery ceilings by reverting to the pre-Montgomery linear game (dlVP-lineage explicit-formula positivity), whose own binding walls -- Vinogradov-Korobov stagnation since 1958 and the visibility currency of Finding 3 -- are older and harder, and are not addressed by either generator. findings.claim: Corollary T2 of the first theorem is false as stated, and the field's central invariant m(a,T) plus its certificate genre hit a provable 1/log T sliver/visibility wall that restores polynomial-in-height prime-data requirements.
findings.argument: T2 claims quasi-RH(a) up to height T is equivalent, up to C1/(a-1/2) collars, to positivity of u on the SEGMENT {sigma = a, |t| <= T}. Counterexample configuration: one zero at rho0 = 0.9 + i*10^6, a = 0.6. On the segment, u(0.6, t) = ambient + plume, ambient ~ (1/2) log(gamma/2pi) ~ 6.0, plume >= -m0/(beta0 - a) = -1/0.3 ~ -3.3, so u > 0 on the entire segment while quasi-RH(0.6) fails badly in the middle of the box -- no edge collar fixes this. What segment-positivity actually certifies is only the sliver beta in (a, a + O(m/log gamma)): a zero forces u < 0 at level a only when beta - a <~ 2m/log gamma (plume depth 1/(beta-a) must beat ambient (1/2) log(gamma/2pi)). Hence a zero-free BOX needs an a-grid of spacing ~1/log T (or a 2-D certificate), and resolving the corresponding plumes (t-width ~ beta-a ~ 1/log T) needs window bandwidth ~ log T, i.e. prime cutoff X >= T^c -- the proposal's own failure-mode 3, but it is not a mere risk: since Int P_x(y) dy = pi independent of depth x, ANY unit-width window sees at most O(1) negative signal from a single off-line zero against ambient ~ (1/2) log T, so single-zero detection above height ~ e^{c' log X} is impossible for the uncorrected instrument; with the residue correction (Finding 1) detection follows the classical X^{beta-a}-vs-density tradeoff instead. Either way the certificate genre has the same resource law as classical EF computations, and its reachable instances (e.g. M3's 'no zeros beta > 0.9, |t| <= 10^3') are numerically subsumed by Platt-Trudgian's verification of RH itself to height 3*10^12; only the genre/Lean novelty survives. Same wall infects the MASTER INEQUALITY: m(a,T) = inf_{|t|<=T} u(a,t) is attained at small t (ambient grows like (1/2) log t; the quoted 0.046(a-1/2) is the low-height bottleneck), so m is blind to off-line zeros at height t0 unless beta - a <~ 2/log t0 -- even a proven margin-propagation inequality for m would not exclude deep zeros at large height without the sliver-scan, i.e. the organizing functional is mis-specified and must be height-localized.

findings.claim: Sector I is structurally capped at the classical (1899) zero-free-region shape: the load-bearing axiom Lambda(n) >= 0 is consumed only by DISCARDING the prime share, so the V-function can never reach Vinogradov-Korobov, let alone enter the strip; the S4 claim 'content scales with bandwidth' is false for Sector I.
findings.argument: In the LP defining V(t,y;L), positivity of pi enters solely to drop the prime term from the budget identity; the resulting bound therefore holds uniformly over ALL positive prime data, so its strength is that of the archimedean-plus-pole terms alone. Quantitatively: for any cone element, 2(what*mu_y)(t) <= 2 sup what <= 2 what(0) = 2 Int w = pole share (using w >= 0, what >= 0, Int mu_y = cosh(0)/cosh(0) = 1), so the defect share NEVER exceeds the pole share and V > 1 requires the archimedean integral to be negative. But mu_inf(tau) = (2pi)^{-1}[Re psi(1/4 + i tau/2) - log pi] is negative only on |tau| <~ 6.3 with fixed O(1) total negative mass (mu_inf(0) ~ -0.855, ~ -0.075 at tau=4, positive ~ log(tau)/2pi beyond), while making (what*mu_y)(t) comparable to what(0) at large height t forces what-mass near +-t, charged +c log t (or +c L for wide elements) by the positive archimedean density; additionally double positivity (w >= 0 AND what >= 0) caps what(t)/what(0) < 1 (the 3-4-1 loss, e.g. 2/3 for the dlVP element). Contradiction therefore requires (1-2y)^{-1} >~ L + log t — the classical shape, which the proposal's own mechanism text concedes ('contradiction requires (1-2delta)^{-1} >~ L + log t'). Increasing L does not deepen the region (the budget charge grows with L), so for fixed interior depth y0 < 1/2, V(t,y0;L) stays < 1 for all L: content does NOT grow toward RH with bandwidth in Sector I, and the Bombieri-vacuity evasion (S4: 'content scales with bandwidth') is true only of Sector II. findings.claim: Prior-art exposure of Sector I is worse than 'possible partial': the classical zero-free-region method literally IS an LP over the double-positivity cone, with an explicit optimization literature; and the claimed dlVP cone element is not actually in Sigma_L.
findings.argument: The classical method optimizes over nonnegative trigonometric polynomials with nonnegative coefficients — precisely {w >= 0, what >= 0} — and its constant-optimization is an established computational literature (Landau's problem; Mossinghoff-Trudgian JNT 2015; Mossinghoff-Trudgian-Yang 2022-24; Kadiri's explicit regions), so M1's 'foundations paper' novelty reduces to the cosh-division/strip-positivity observation, the mu_y depth-kernel calculus (which I verified: the closed form is exact, ratio 4*pi across y in [0, 0.4] and xi, reducing to (1/2)sech(pi xi) at y=0), and the abstract-datum calibration. Also: w(u) = e^{-a|u|}(1 + cos tu)^2 is NOT compactly supported, so the dlVP '3-4-1' element lies only in a degenerate limit of Sigma_L, and the formalized explicit formula (WeilEF) covers only compactly supported C^2 tests (map-hooks: compact support is load-bearing) — the 'contains dlVP' claim needs a limiting argument outside the current formal class. The proposal flags the prior-art risk itself (failure mode 1), which is why this is minor rather than major.

findings.claim: The numerics campaign cannot test the headline t-aspect improvement, and the Lean hook understates the Gevrey infrastructure lift.
findings.argument: The claimed 'exponential improvement in the t-aspect' (threshold delta^{-1} loglog t vs the transcript's sqrt(log t)/delta) is numerically indistinguishable at all reachable heights: for t in [10^3, 10^10], loglog t ranges over [1.9, 3.1] and sqrt(log t) over [2.6, 4.8] — both O(1) constants absorbed into C. Only the delta-aspect (delta^{-1} vs the transcript's measured delta^{-0.07}) is discriminable, so M2's promised comparison against the L*_ann law tests one axis of two; the t-aspect claim will rest entirely on the proof. Secondarily, M4's plan to 'extend Zeta23/Tail from C^3 to Gevrey tapers' presumes Denjoy-Carleman/Gevrey function theory that does not exist in Mathlib; building it is a serious formalization project, not an extension. Honest audit disclosures on the other side: (a) the mu_y kernel calculus checks out exactly; (b) the master identity is a correct rearrangement of Riemann-Weil with genuine termwise nonnegativity on the cone; (c) I attempted to kill the first theorem's parameter architecture on the grounds that width-L Gevrey-alpha edges would destroy the cosh gain for alpha < 2, and the attempt FAILED: numerically measured edge-flatness penalty exponent is ~1/alpha (0.70 measured vs 0.67 predicted at alpha=1.5; 0.54 vs 0.50 at alpha=2), i.e. exp(-c(delta L)^{1/alpha}), sublinear in delta L, so the stated margin delta^2 e^{(1-c0) delta L}, radius R = C0 L^{alpha-1}, and threshold L >= C0 delta^{-1}(loglog t + log(1/delta)) are mutually consistent, and the balance arithmetic (defect delta^2 e^{delta L}(delta L)^{-2k-2} vs in-window C log t/L^2) is correct. The first theorem is very likely provable as stated.

findings.claim: The central zero-side identity is mathematically wrong: tr(G_a G_b G_c) has CROSS-window kernels with Fourier supports min(lambda_i, lambda_j), not the claimed per-window kernels Phi_w with supports lambda_w. The headline 'mixed-window corner with one factor at pair-bandwidth ~1' does not exist in the proposed construction.
findings.argument: In tr(G_aG_bG_c) = Sum_{k1k2k3}(G_a)_{k1k2}(G_b)_{k2k3}(G_c)_{k3k1}, the shared grid index k2 pairs the right slot of G_a with the left slot of G_b. The k2-sum is Sum_{k2} conj(phihat_a(gbar1 - tau_k2)) phihat_b(g2 - tau_k2); Poisson over the grid of spacing 2pi/l gives l*(phi_a phi_b)^hat(g2 - gbar1) (exact since (lambda_a+lambda_b)l/2 < l). The u-integrand is the PRODUCT phi_a*phi_b, supported in the INTERSECTION of supports, so the kernel bandwidth is min(lambda_a, lambda_b). The proposal's formula 'l^3 Sum m1m2m3 Phi_a(g1-g2)Phi_b(g2-g3)Phi_c(g3-g1)' with Phi_w = (phi_w^2)^hat, and the support claim '{xi1+xi2+xi3=0, |xi_w| <= lambda_w}', are both false unless all windows are equal (the quoted Poisson identity is a same-window identity, but adjacent factors in the trace pair DIFFERENT windows). Consequence: the accessible triple-kernel supports are (s1,s2,s3) = (min(a,b), min(b,c), min(c,a)). Maximizing s1+s2+s3 subject to a+b+c < 2, all <= 1 (WLOG a<=b<=c, total = 2a+b) forces a=b=c: the total-support-2 boundary is attained ONLY at equal windows 2/3 — exactly the corner the parent paper already names (kLambda < 2, k=3). At the proposal's flagship point (0.98, 0.5, 0.5) the kernels have supports (0.5, 0.5, 0.5), total 1.5 — strictly LESS information than equal windows at 2/3, and no factor anywhere near pair-bandwidth 1. Getting s1 -> 1 would need lambda_a = lambda_b -> 1, forcing lambda_c < 0. So T1 as stated (connected-triple vanishing on the full sigma < 2 simplex via this construction) is wrongly derived, novelty claim (1) and the PairCeiling-evasion mechanism ('degree-3 rows carrying one bandwidth-1 direction') collapse, and this is consistent with the artifact's own scoping (tr G^k available for k*lambda < 2 — the paper's equal-window boundary is not an oversight but the true optimum of this construction). A repair exists — two-slot non-Hermitian G_w = W(phi_w^L e_{tau_k}, phi_w^R e_{tau_l}) with slot budget Sum_w(lambda_w^L + lambda_w^R)/2 < 2 reaches the full simplex s1+s2+s3 < 2 including (1-eps, 0.49, 0.49) — but it destroys Hermiticity, and the entire certificate side (Sylvester inertia, n_+, Schur-Jensen, rank_trace_cubic) requires Hermitian compressions. So the repaired T1 survives only as a standalone correlation theorem; the certificate arm is confined to the equal-window <= 2/3 box.

findings.claim: The proposal's own first formalizable statement, rank_trace_cubic, is FALSE as stated: explicit counterexamples with zero block trace-asymmetry violate it unboundedly for any c3 < 0. The interaction currency needed to repair it has no prime-side evaluation — this is the G1-G4 'free mass mover' failure one degree up, and at odd degree there is no positivity to fall back on.
findings.argument: Stated target: for P = Sum m_j v_j v_j^dagger, Q Hermitian = sum of blocks B_i with n_+(B_i) <= 1, any weights with psi(m) <= 1 (forcing c3 <= 0): Sum psi(m_j) + q(c)b >= c1 tr A + c2 tr A^2 + c3 tr A^3 - R, with R <= eps*tr A^2 + C(eps)*(block trace-asymmetries). Counterexample: P = 0; B_i = mu(e_i e_i^dagger - w w^dagger), i = 1..p, with orthonormal e_i and w orthogonal to all e_i. Each B_i has eigenvalues {+mu, -mu}, n_+(B_i) = 1, tr B_i = 0 (zero asymmetry). Q = mu*Sum e_ie_i^dagger - p*mu*ww^dagger has spectrum {+mu (x p), -p*mu}: tr A = 0, tr A^2 = (p + p^2)mu^2, tr A^3 = (p - p^3)mu^3 < 0. For any c3 < 0 the RHS contains |c3|(p^3-p)mu^3 while LHS = q(c)p is fixed and R <= eps(p+p^2)mu^2 + 0; letting mu -> infinity violates the inequality. If one objects that zeta-blocks have the outer-product form m(uw^dagger + wu^dagger) (under which shared-w blocks collapse to a single harmless hyperbolic pair), take two blocks with shared amplified direction u1 = u2 and misaligned damped directions (w2 perp w1, <w2,u1> = -t): tr(B1^2 B2) = ||w1||^2 * 2Re(<u1,u2><w2,u1>) * mu^3-scale = -2t*mu^3 — signed cross terms of size mu^3 with all block traces zero. Realizable-shaped: off-line zeros at nearby heights have substantially overlapping evaluation vectors (the transcript's cluster-visibility remark), and sign/alignment is adversary-tunable via positions. The abstract zero-side layer ('contains no arithmetic', arbitrary reflection-invariant multisets — the architecture the Lean formalization is built on) must admit these configurations, so the lemma needs either (i) a new hypothesis tying u_i to w_i geometrically — configuration-localization input that the invariant list cannot express and whose verification at zeta is blocked by the visibility/interference wall — or (ii) an interaction remainder containing signed cross-block cubic overlaps, which have NO prime-side evaluation: the prime side computes only the three traces, and at degree 3 the global trace does not one-sidedly bound individual pieces because odd-degree terms carry signs. This is the precise structural reason degree 2 works (||A||_F^2 is a sum of squares, so the global MV-bounded second moment automatically caps every block's X^{2y} mass, making n_+-only pricing valid) and degree 3 cannot: 'the zero-side second moment cannot be read termwise' becomes, at degree 3, 'the cubic cannot be read termwise AND has no positive global reading'. Generic Schatten-Holder gives |tr(ABC)| <= prod ||.||_{S3} <= prod ||.||_{S2} ~ (kappa N)^{3/2} = N^{3/2}, useless for o(N) accounting; any better split needs an operator-norm bound — the repo's named Lindelof lock. The proposal's evasion ('c3 <= 0 means mass escaping to large eigenvalues only hurts the adversary') addresses only the ON-LINE large-m escape (the LP-dual odd-moment no-go); the off-line signed-interaction escape is the actual killer and is untouched. M3 and hence M4's headline (beating 0.6818287, improving 5/6) are dead as designed.

findings.claim: M1 prices an unobtainable data class: triple rows on the full simplex j1+j2 <= N, when the certificate-compatible (Hermitian) construction only reaches the box j1, j2, j1+j2 <= (2/3)N — and the deleted rows are precisely the plausibly-binding ones (near-edge triples taxing the 256-law's edge atom). The decision gate can pass spuriously and the predicted range 0.69-0.73 is unfounded.
findings.argument: By finding 1, provable triple data for Hermitian compressions lives at kernel supports <= 2/3 per direction, i.e. LP rows A3(j1,j2) with j1, j2, j1+j2 <= (2/3)N — about 44% of the proposed row region, and crucially excluding all rows with j1+j2 in ((2/3)N, N). The 256-law's entire advantage lives in the free edge row j = N (atom mass ~0.826 per the Lean ceiling analysis); the triple rows that would most plausibly tax that structure are those coupling in-band frequencies to near-edge ones (j1 + j2 close to N, constraining F(j1)F(j2)conj(F(j1+j2)) against the edge atom) — exactly the unreachable region. On the honest box, CUE-vanishing triple constraints are weak (satisfied by CUE and small perturbations; the adversary re-optimizes positions to decohere in-box triangle correlations while keeping pair rows and the edge/double structure), so p0^(3) ~ p0^(2) is the likely honest outcome. Running M1 as specified would produce a gate decision about a data class no theorem in the program can deliver. Repair: re-scope rows to the attainable region (or to the region of the non-Hermitian repaired T1, if a consumption mechanism for non-Hermitian mixed traces is ever found — none is proposed), and inflate tau3 near the attainable boundary to reflect T1's error blowup (the proposal's own failure mode 3).

findings.claim: The Alternative-Hypothesis payoff (M6, and obstruction-evasion item 2) is empty: AH-structured laws do not violate connected-triple vanishing anywhere in the provable range, so the 'obstruction converted into a target' argument fails.
findings.argument: For half-integer-lattice (AH-structured) configurations, the triple observable A3(j1,j2) = Re[F(j1)F(j2)conj(F(j1+j2))]/N is large only when all three frequencies sit near dual-lattice resonances. The minimal non-degenerate triple resonances involve total support >= 2: e.g. (1/2, 1/2, -1) has |xi1|+|xi2|+|xi3| = 2, sitting exactly ON the closed-simplex boundary that every version of T1 excludes (T1 is an open-simplex sigma < 2 statement, and the proposal's own LP leaves edges free); full dual-lattice triples like (2,2,-4) are far outside. Inside the open total-support-<2 simplex — a fortiori inside the honest 2/3-box of finding 3 — AH laws SATISFY the triple-vanishing rows. This matches the known pattern (AH is precisely engineered to be consistent with all bandwidth-1 pair data; its deviations begin at the support boundary): the natural extension is that AH is consistent with all restricted-range n-level data, and the proposal provides no computation to the contrary. The claim that 'rigid arithmetic spacings generate triple resonances j1+j2=j3 in-band' is backwards: the resonances exist but are out of band. M6's 'potential first refutation of AH' — billed as 'the most significant pair-correlation-adjacent result since Montgomery' — should be expected to return the null result, and evasion item 2 loses its content.

findings.claim: Section 7.5(g) is overread as an 'existence proof that cubic accounting survives interactions': the cited RH-conditional result has Q EMPTY, so it demonstrates nothing about the interactions that actually kill Lemma C.
findings.argument: Under RH there are no off-line zeros: A = P, all mass is on-line, the matrix is PSD, and the Schur-Horn majorization argument of 7.5(g) (f(x) = -x^2/9 + x^3/18, N_d >= 0.85082) never faces a hyperbolic block, an X^{2y}-amplified eigenvalue, or a signed P-Q cross term. The interactions it 'survives' are on-line/on-line only — and even at degree 2 the campaign record shows the spectral (m-1)(m-2) level is destroyed by on-line interactions under RH+GUE, recovered only by the regrouping device, which is inherently quadratic (it relies on Frobenius positivity). The proposal half-admits this ('Lemma C is its unconditional extension with Q nonempty') but then uses 7.5(g) as evidence for exactly the step (off-line interaction control at odd degree) on which 7.5(g) is silent. Combined with finding 2, the honest statement is: there exists NO evidence, conditional or numerical, that cubic accounting survives Q-interactions, and there is a concrete counterexample class showing the proposed form does not.

findings.claim: Assorted mechanism slips: tr(G_aG_bG_c) is not real in general and must be symmetrized; the same-prime-power triple diagonal is O(1/l^3)-relative, not O(1/l); endpoint loglog/log losses at lambda_a -> 1 (admitted) interact badly with a gain the proposal itself estimates could be ~0.01.
findings.argument: (i) For non-commuting Hermitian A,B,C, conj(tr(ABC)) = tr(CBA) != tr(ABC); the certificate row must be Re tr(G_aG_bG_c) or the symmetrized sum over both cyclic orders — never stated, fixable, but it changes the LP observable (the proposal's A3 rows do take Re and Im, so the analytic side and the LP side are currently pricing different functionals). (ii) The exact-relation term n1n2 = n3 forces all three to be powers of one prime: Sum_p (log p)^3 Sum_{a,b} p^{-a-b} converges to O(1), contributing O(T) against the main term T*l^3, i.e. relative O(1/l^3); the stated O(1/l) is off by two logs (conservative direction, harmless, but indicates the error bookkeeping in the Mechanism was not carried through). (iii) The proposal's own failure-mode list concedes p0^(3) - 0.6725 might be ~0.01 while the lambda_a -> 1 endpoint erosion is loglog/log — at T-ranges where the parent certificate is barely positive, a 0.01 headline gain is inside the endpoint noise; no quantitative reconciliation is offered.

verdicts.repairs: Three genuinely salvageable pieces, none of which is the thesis. (1) T1 as a standalone theorem: restate with the correct cross-window kernels. Two honest versions: (a) equal windows lambda < 2/3 (Hermitian, kernel supports (lambda,lambda,lambda), total < 2) — the corrected form of what the paper's 7.5(e) sketches, still the first unconditional order-3 correlation theorem for zeta (BGSTB is order 2), publishable; (b) the stronger repair: two-slot non-Hermitian compressions G_w = W(phi_w^L e_{tau_k}, phi_w^R e_{tau_l}); the slot windows pair cyclically, giving kernel supports s1 = min(lam_a^R, lam_b^L) etc., and setting lam_a^R = lam_b^L = s1 (cyclically) makes the prime-side budget Sum_w (lam^L + lam^R)/2 = s1+s2+s3 < 2 — the FULL Rudnick-Sarnak simplex, including one direction at bandwidth 1-eps, becomes reachable unconditionally. This repaired M2 is the real prize of the direction and survives all findings — but it feeds no known certificate (non-Hermitian products have no inertia/Schur-Jensen machinery). (2) M1 re-scoped: run the triple-row LP on the attainable region only (box j1,j2,j1+j2 <= (2/3)N for the Hermitian class), with edge-inflated tolerances; also run the AH-structured configurations expecting the null result, and separately run the full-simplex LP purely as an upper bound on what ANY future consumption mechanism could buy. Publish either outcome as the order-3 extension of the PairCeiling meta-theorem. The pair-only dual at N=128 (candidate certificate for the 0.6725 -> 0.6818 gap) is independent of every finding here and worth extracting regardless. (3) If a certificate arm is ever revived, the missing ingredient identified by finding 2 is a prime-side-computable POSITIVE interaction currency; one concrete candidate the proposal misses: mixed quartic traces tr(G_aG_bG_bG_a) = ||G_bG_a||_F^2 >= 0, unconditionally evaluable when the slot budget is < 2 (e.g. lambda_a = 0.7, lambda_b = 0.29), giving a sign-definite fourth-order functional that upper-bounds cross-window interaction mass — even-degree positivity at total support < 2 is the only visible route around the odd-degree sign problem, and it should be priced by the LP before any analytic work. Do not attempt rank_trace_cubic in its stated form; any restatement must carry vector-geometry hypotheses (u-w coupling of realizable blocks) and a proof they instantiate at zeta, which is a new open problem adjacent to the visibility wall.

findings.claim: The depth dictionary sigma_death ~ a^2/2 is wrong for a >~ 2: the mean-field attraction of the real-zero sea makes complex-pair death time LINEAR in depth, so the flagship depth-resolved numbers (0.0317N at a=3, 0.0041N at a=5, ~2N/a^4 tail) are unobtainable; the true certificate-reachable curve is ~J_+(c*a)/2 ~ N/(2c^2 a^2).
findings.argument: Under the forward flow dH/dt = -H'', zeros obey zdot_k = 2*sum'_{j} 1/(z_k - z_j). For a complex zero at z = x + iy above real zeros x_j of density rho, each real zero contributes Im[2/(z-x_j)] = -2y/((x-x_j)^2 + y^2) < 0 to ydot; in the continuum limit the sum is -2*pi*rho, INDEPENDENT of y once y >> spacing Delta. With H_0's z-coordinate density rho = L/(4*pi) (Delta = 4*pi/L), ydot = -1/y - L/2 + O(fluctuations): the herding term -L/2 exceeds the isolated-pair term -1/y = -L/(2a) (y = 2a/L) precisely when a > 1, so death occurs at t ~ 2y/L = 4a/L^2, i.e. sigma_death ~ a (LINEAR), not a^2/2. Numerical integration of the actual ODE (frozen lattice, run above) confirms: t_death/(y^2/2) = 0.42 at y = Delta/2 (a ~ 3), 0.24 at y = Delta (a ~ 6.3), 0.07 at y = 2*Delta, asymptoting to y/(2*pi*rho). Cross-checks: (i) this is exactly Polymath15's effective-shift heuristic (H_t behaves like the completed zeta with Re s shifted by ~t*L/4, linear in t — the mechanism of their barrier), which the proposal's own failure-mode note says it failed to reconcile; (ii) it reproduces the KKL picture that complex zeros of H_t at fixed t survive only below height ~e^{C/t} (linear law: depth 1/2 dies at t ~ 2/L, i.e. survives only for L <~ 2/t) — the quadratic law would instead predict survival to t ~ 1/8 at ALL heights, contradicting KKL's finiteness; (iii) no conflict with de Bruijn's y(t)^2 <= y(0)^2 - 2t, which is only an UPPER bound on survival, attained by an isolated pair — the proposal silently promoted this one-sided maximum principle to a two-sided death law. Quantitative damage (verified numerically): at a=3 the claimed bound J_+(4.5)/2 = 0.0317N becomes at best J_+(~1.9)/2 ~ 0.079N; at a=5, claimed 0.0041N becomes >= 0.027N even with the most optimistic constant c=1; the large-a tail is a^{-2}, not a^{-4}. This also moves the honest crossover against Selberg/Fujii-type critical-zone density bounds (N*e^{-ca}) sharply downward: the novelty window shrinks to a = O(1), where the improvement over the flat 1/6 is real but modest (J_+'(0)/2 = -1/15 per unit sigma: bound ~ 1/6 - c*a/15).

findings.claim: The configuration-free per-pair survival LOWER bound (M2's dynamical lemma) is impossible at diffusive scale, not merely hard: unconditional zero-counting allows S(t)-size clusters that herd a deep pair to the axis in time o(1/L^2), so the unconditional zeta transfer as stated fails; only a proportion-form repair with an exceptional set (priced by the certified form factor) can survive.
findings.argument: The depth-resolved corollary needs: every zeta pair at depth >= a/L is still complex at t = 4*sigma/L^2 for sigma up to ~sigma_death(a). A survival lower bound requires an upper bound on descent speed, i.e. an upper bound on the local zero count near the pair. Unconditionally, N(tau+h) - N(tau) = (h/2pi)*log(tau/2pi) + O(log tau), and the O(log tau) term (S(t)) is not improvable below ~log tau: a window of length y = 2a/L may contain up to C*L zeros. A cluster of K zeros within distance ~y of the pair produces descent speed ~2K/y; with K ~ C*L this is C*L^2/a, giving death time ~ y/(C L^2/a) = O(a^2/L^3) = o(diffusive time 1/L^2). So there is NO per-pair survival lemma valid against all configurations satisfying the method's inputs — exactly the pattern of the campaign's Part-I 'no configuration-free visibility theorem', which the proposal itself cites as a warning and hedges with a fallback ('zeta transfer under a mild local-density hypothesis'), conceding the headline word 'unconditional' for the zeta-side bound. The repair that CAN plausibly restore unconditionality is not stated in the proposal: shrouding c*N deep pairs with O(1)-size clusters perturbs the pair-correlation form factor by O(c) across the band, which the certified (M1) form factor F_t = damped + o(1) excludes for fixed c; and the number of 1/L-windows holding >= K zeros is <= C*N/K^2 by the bandwidth-one second moment. This converts the per-pair claim into a proportion statement with an exceptional set of size O(N/K^2) and degraded constants — a genuinely different (and weaker) theorem than the one advertised in the thesis and payoff sections.

findings.claim: The M4 equivalence [diffusive flow-realness for all sigma] <=> [narrow-box hypothesis] fails in the stated clean form in its (=>) direction, for the same reason as Finding 2; it degrades to an equivalence under a local-density side condition or with positive-proportion/exceptional-set caveats.
findings.argument: The (<=) direction (NB => diffusive realness) is plausible: real-sea herding and vertical collapse (in the ODE zdot = 2*sum' 1/(z-z_j), vertically separated zeros ATTRACT: for z_top - z_low = i*h, ydot_top = -2/h — so no screening tower of complex pairs can sustain a zero above the diffusive death scale, and heat-kernel locality handles zeros outside the window). But the (=>) direction needs: if depth >= eps/L occurs infinitely often, some such pair SURVIVES to sigma ~ eps^2 — a survival lower bound. If the deep zeros are o(N) in number, they can all be cluster-shrouded at zero form-factor cost (the O(c) budget argument of Finding 2 only protects positive proportions), and then they die before any fixed sigma, making H_t all-real in windows even though NB fails. The proposal says 'modulo the M2 survival lemma', which is honest, but since the configuration-free M2 lemma is impossible (Finding 2), the clean equivalence is unrecoverable; what survives is 'diffusive realness <=> NB' under a mild density hypothesis, or with NB replaced by a positive-proportion narrow-box statement. This matters because the M4 payoff ('RH cleanly stratified into diffusive layer = NB + fixed-t residue') is the proposal's main conceptual claim.

findings.claim: The M3 'edge-atom flow-invariance' analysis misidentifies where the joint-sigma LP's action is: the decisive effect is the doubles' splitting signature (an O(sigma) band-edge-region deviation the 256-law cannot avoid), and Outcome A hinges on an unposed realizability question — whether the adversary's FREE 3-point structure can cancel that signature within point-process positivity.
findings.argument: Under forward flow the 256-law's mass-1/6 doubles split into real pairs at separation s = sqrt(8*sigma)/L = 0.225*sqrt(sigma)*Delta, contributing 2 + 2*cos(2*pi*alpha*s/Delta) instead of 4 to pair rows — a deviation of order sigma*alpha^2 that does NOT vanish at alpha -> 1 (at sigma = 1, alpha = 1 the phase is 1.41 rad, a ~40% change in each double's edge-region contribution, total O(1/6 * sigma) in the rows), whereas the certified damping multiplier e^{-2*sigma*alpha*(1-alpha)} DOES vanish at alpha = 1. So the flowed 256-law generically FAILS the certified rows at order sigma exactly in the edge region where its advantage (the free 0.826 atom) lives — the flow rows are stronger against the specific 256-law than the proposal's own 'edge atom is flow-invariant' caveat suggests. The adversary cannot dodge by replacing doubles with band-indistinguishable objects: close real pairs are SIMPLE (destroying the low-simple-fraction objective) and off-line pairs at depth a contribute cosh(2*alpha*a)-type factors (band-visible unless a << 1, in which case they split like doubles at diffusive times anyway). The only escape is tuning the higher correlations of the simple 5/6 mass — unconstrained by bandwidth-one data — so that its O(sigma) flow response cancels the doubles' signature; whether a bona fide point process realizes this (positivity of correlation hierarchies) is the actual content of M3, and the proposal neither poses it nor prices it. Net: M3 remains a legitimate open computation (as claimed), but both the proposal's pessimistic argument (edge invariance) and its optimistic framing (LP over depth/multiplicity profiles with transport rows — which linearizes away exactly the 3-point freedom that decides the question) are off-target; the numerics item (3) as designed (flowing marked configurations and re-solving with damped rows) would produce evidence, not a theorem, in Outcome A.

findings.claim: M1's mechanism survives audit — the multiplier algebra, the kappa_sigma structure (undamped delta term + damped form-factor term), all quoted constants, sigma* = 2.6569, and the Polymath15 exponent shape all check out — but the effective explicit formula for H_t at the lambda -> 1 endpoint remains a heavy, unproven analytic debt, and the theorem should be claimed at fixed lambda < 1 first, as the proposal's own mitigation states.
findings.argument: Verified independently: (i) the stationary-phase multiplier m_n = e^{(t/4)((theta'-log n)^2 - theta'^2)} = e^{(t/4) log n (log n - L)} = e^{-sigma*alpha*(1-alpha)} at t = 4*sigma/L^2 is algebraically correct (mode of z-frequency u gets e^{t u^2}; term n has z-frequency (theta'(gamma) - log n)/2; chirp-width and theta-curvature corrections are O(sigma/L), absorbable); it matches my recollection of Polymath15's B_t coefficients b_n^t = exp((t/4) log^2(N_0/n)) with log N_0 = L/2, resolving the reconciliation the designer says failed from memory — in the proposal's FAVOR; (ii) kappa_sigma(lambda) correctly leaves the 1/lambda zero-self-pairing delta term undamped and damps only the prime-diagonal |alpha|-part — the right structure per the Montgomery F(alpha) decomposition; (iii) numerically R(0.117)=0.68188, R(0.761)=0.75330, R(1.98)=0.84529, R(3.17)=0.89982, sigma*=2.6569, sigma^2*J_+ -> 1, all matching the proposal to the stated digits; (iv) MV off-diagonal with |Lambda_t| <= e^{sigma/4}*Lambda inflates constants only. Remaining genuine debt: an effective EF for H_t with Landau/rectangle machinery needs growth and zero-strip control for H_t (available: de Bruijn strip forward, Gaussian-convolution representation backward, Jensen log-density) plus Polymath15-grade effective approximation UNIFORM as t -> 0 — plausible since t -> 0 approaches classical Riemann-Siegel, but the endpoint-admissibility (parent Remark 6.1 analogue) at lambda -> 1 with inflated constants is unverified. No hidden Lindelof/density-strength input detected anywhere in the M1 chain. The fixed-lambda < 1 fallback (R(sigma,lambda) = 2 - 1/lambda - J(sigma,lambda)) is sound and should be the actual first theorem.

verdicts.repairs: (1) Replace the depth dictionary by the two-regime law sigma_death(a) ~ min(a^2/2, c*a) with an explicit herding constant c (from descent speed 1/y + 2*pi*rho_local, rho >= unconditional real-zero density); rederive the depth curve as J_+(sigma_death(a))/2 ~ a^{-2}, and redo the Selberg/Fujii comparison honestly — the novelty window is a = O(1), where the bound reads ~1/6 - c*a/15. (2) Restate M2's zeta transfer as a proportion theorem with exceptional set: pairs shrouded by K-clusters number O(N/K^2) by the bandwidth-one second moment, and shrouding a positive proportion c*N of deep pairs distorts the certified F_t by O(c), which the flowed-BGSTB theorem excludes; abandon the configuration-free per-pair lemma (it is impossible — S(t)-size clusters kill it). Alternatively keep the clean per-pair form explicitly conditional on a local-density hypothesis. (3) M4: state the equivalence with the density-hypothesis caveat or with NB in positive-proportion form; drop 'cleanly stratified' from the payoff. (4) M3: replace the edge-atom-invariance discussion with the doubles-splitting-signature analysis (the O(sigma) edge-region deviation of split doubles vs the vanishing damping at alpha=1) and pose the real question: can a point-process law's free 3-point structure cancel the splitting signature within correlation-positivity? Add this as an explicit row-set in the LP probe. (5) Prove M1 first at fixed lambda < 1; treat the lambda -> 1 endpoint and the t-uniform effective approximation as separate verifiable propositions. With these repairs the direction's deliverables — the R(sigma) family, flowed BGSTB, backward-side theorem, a weakened-but-first unconditional depth-resolved proportion bound, the M3 probe, and the fourth Lean instantiation — all stand.
